chunks: Take care of the affairs of those of them who do not approach you, among those whom the eyes look at with contempt and whom people regard as low.
Appoint for them some trusted people who are God-fearing and humble, so that they may inform you of their conditions.
Then deal with them with a sense of responsibility to Allāh on the day you will meet Him,
because these people, among the subjects, are more in need of equitable treatment than others.
And for each one, render account to Allāh in fulfilling his right.
ai.seo_question: How should a ruler treat the poor and marginalized according to Imam Ali's instructions to Malik al-Ashtar?
ai.summary: This directive highlights the Shia political principle of 'adl' (justice) by prioritizing the 'fuqara' (poor/marginalized) who lack the means to petition authority, a concept central to Imam Ali's governance model. It underscores the governor's personal accountability ('muhasaba') for ensuring these vulnerable groups receive their due rights, reflecting the theological link between earthly administration and divine judgment.
